newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich says budget talks with Clinton useful.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich says budget talks with Clinton useful.

text.p: House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich said on Tuesday that a meeting with President Bill Clinton on the budget was very useful, saying that there was broad agreement on many areas.

"It was a very useful meeting," Gingrich told reporters after the White House session, which included the Republican leaders of Congress and their Democratic counterparts. "Most of the discussion was positive, in a very constructive way."
Gingrich said there was broad agreement in a number of areas, but he offered no details.
"We want to make sure that there is a tax cut for working families and for their children, the $500 tax credit. I think there is a broad agreement," he said, without elaborating.
Gingrich alluded to progress on cutting the capital gains tax, but again without offering any detail.
"We want to make sure that people who create jobs by saving and by investing have a tax break to increase economic growth and I think there's a broad agreement now on that," he said.

"We want to ensure that family farms and small businesses are not destroyed by the IRS because of death tax and I think there's agreement there," he added in an apparent reference to plans to restructure the inheritance tax.

Other particpants in the meeting, which included Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott and the leaders of the Democratic minority, suggested that the meeting was designed not so much as a negotiating session as an airing of views.

Asked if the two sides had moved toward each other, Senate Minority Leader Tom Dashle said: "I don't think this meeting was designed for movement, per se. It was designed for both sides to talk about where their priorities are as we go into serious negotiations now in the next two weeks."
He was referring to a congressional "conference" that began last week and aims to resolve differences between the House and Senate balanced budget legislation.
"Our goal is to finish by the end of the month. I think we can accomplish that," Daschle added.
